markdown_report:
The best first step is a controlled history-intervention diagnostic adapter. At 0% progress, establishing trustworthy measurements is more useful than adding an unvalidated compatibility reranker. No benchmark improvement is claimed.

**Insights from the starting point.** First, existing margins aggregate training positions; they cannot establish final-position recommendation quality. Diagnose the final user representation separately. Second, raw margins depend on score scale, while mean embedding cosine does not uniquely identify collapse. Add ranking-based measurements and describe existing metrics narrowly. Third, qualitative feedback suggests excessive reliance on isolated purchases, but actual intent and equipment ownership remain unobserved. History interventions can test model dependence without asserting either.

**Insights from related work.** First, FCESR distinguishes necessity from sufficiency: removal and retention answer different questions [1]. Both are needed to characterize history dependence. Second, recency research motivates controlled temporal probes [2]. Comparisons must match intervention size and recency to avoid attributing ordinary deletion damage to repeated-interest evidence. Third, complementary recommendation research separates substitutes from complements [3]. Textual similarity alone therefore cannot establish redundancy or compatibility.

**Directions and framework.** Organize work along three axes: measurement reliability, history dependence, and evidence-supported item relations. The corresponding framework is: observational probes → controlled interventions → optional model changes; each stage requires stronger evidence. Missing specifications remain unknown, and only pinned validation HR@10 selects models.

**Candidate ideas.** Scores are originality/potential/difficulty, each out of 10; higher difficulty means harder implementation.

- **Controlled history audit: 4/8/3.** Originality: useful integration (+), established intervention methods (−). Potential: identifies actionable dependence (+), diagnostic changes may not predict accuracy (−). Difficulty: existing inference hooks suffice (+), careful position controls are necessary (−). References: [1,2].
- **Recurrence-conditioned residual pooling: 5/7/5.** Blend SASRec’s final state with a learned pool of recurring-history embeddings. Originality: targeted combination (+), familiar pooling machinery (−). Potential: may recover sustained interests (+), repetition may reflect routine purchases (−). Difficulty: small architecture change (+), predictor and adapter must also change (−). Reference: [2].
- **Explicit-conflict reranking: 4/6/7.** Penalize only text-supported conflicts. Originality: evidence abstention helps (+), rule-based reranking is established (−). Potential: targets concrete mismatches (+), sparse specifications limit coverage (−). Difficulty: simple scoring integration (+), reliable extraction is demanding (−). Reference: [3].

**Selected algorithm.** For fixed training users, compare removal and retention of repeated item IDs against size-matched random subsets, additionally matching recency where feasible. Use position-preserving masking and separately report deletion/repacking. Compare original top-10 retention and rank changes on fixed candidates; these measure model dependence, not preference accuracy. Restore model mode and report empty samples as unavailable. Preserve the twenty-user full-catalog panel separately. Any subsequent model modification must earn selection through four-category macro validation HR@10.

References: [1] https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.13632; [2] https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.09722; [3] https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.16135.

idea.description: Implement a mode-safe, controlled history-intervention audit through the existing DiagnosisProbe interface, retaining current metrics and adding final-position ranking measurements.
idea.motivation: The qualitative diagnosis suggests unsupported broad associations and overweighted isolated interactions. Existing training-position margins cannot distinguish these hypotheses. Controlled interventions provide a feasible initial investigation without assuming latent user traits or unavailable product attributes.
idea.implementation_notes: Retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device) and run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), returning metrics and metric_definitions. Access the trained module through view.model; save and restore its training flag in a finally block. Preserve legacy measurements with precise definitions, sample counts, and unavailable values for empty samples. Use training histories only and deterministic intervention sampling. Define repetition initially through exact item recurrence; report eligible-user coverage because deduplicated histories may contain no repeated IDs. Optional title-based grouping must be labeled a similarity proxy and audited separately. Score the final nonpadding position, holding candidate IDs and eligibility filters fixed across interventions. Distinguish masking from deletion/repacking and document SASRec's handling of internal padding. Retention probes require separate controls because retaining fewer items changes context size. Keep all four dataset routes, DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, and artifacts beneath the trial directory. No inference architecture changes are required for this diagnostic. Preserve the pinned validation evaluator and the separate twenty-user full-catalog recommendation panel. The supplied citations motivate the design; no experiments or source verification were performed here.
idea.pseudocode:
def run_full_diagnosis(self, train_loader):
    was_training = self.view.model.training
    try:
        self.view.model.eval()
        with torch.no_grad():
            metrics = existing_probes_with_counts(train_loader)
            for user in deterministic_training_user_sample(seed=42):
                history = training_history(user)
                candidates = fixed_eligible_candidates(user, seed=42)
                baseline = score_final_state(history, candidates)
                repeated_positions = exact_recurrence_positions(history)
                if not repeated_positions:
                    record_ineligible(user)
                    continue
                controls = matched_random_subsets(
                    history, repeated_positions,
                    match_size=True, match_recency_when_feasible=True)
                for operation in ['mask', 'delete_repack', 'retain']:
                    targeted = intervene(history, repeated_positions, operation)
                    targeted_change = ranking_change(
                        baseline, score_final_state(targeted, candidates))
                    control_changes = []
                    for positions in controls:
                        altered = intervene(history, positions, operation)
                        control_changes.append(ranking_change(
                            baseline, score_final_state(altered, candidates)))
                    record_paired_difference(targeted_change, control_changes)
            return summarize_with_coverage(metrics), metric_definitions
    finally:
        self.view.model.train(was_training)

# Model selection remains external to this diagnostic:
# equal-weight mean of the four pinned category validation HR@10 values.

originality.positive: Combines necessity, sufficiency, temporal controls, and benchmark-compatible diagnostic contracts in a targeted adapter.
originality.negative: The intervention techniques are established; the contribution is careful integration.

future_potential.positive: Can identify reproducible failure hypotheses and guide later architecture or training changes.
future_potential.negative: History sensitivity does not establish user intent or guarantee validation improvement.

code_difficulty.positive: Reuses existing embeddings, sequence encoding, scoring hooks, and public histories.
code_difficulty.negative: Position handling, sparse repetition coverage, and matched controls require careful implementation.

related_work.title: FCESR (2025)
contributions: The supplied summary distinguishes history-subset sufficiency from removal-based necessity.
limitations: Model dependence under intervention does not establish real-world causal preferences.

related_work.title: Measuring Recency Bias (2024)
contributions: The supplied summary motivates measuring excessive recency dependence in sequential recommendation.
limitations: Its reported findings do not establish that reducing recency improves this four-category benchmark.

related_work.title: Complementary Recommendation in E-commerce (2024)
contributions: Distinguishes substitution from complementarity and discusses asymmetric item relationships.
limitations: Does not supply missing compatibility specifications or establish user-level redundancy from purchases alone.
